sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 1005 ± 225.2 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Stable integration in U-2 OS cells confirmed; surface display is the design purpose of HiBiT-FZD constructs. Direct functional assay (e.g., Wnt ligand binding) was demonstrated for HiBiT-FZD5 in the same study (L4) but NOT explicitly reported for FZD2 in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: The construct name 'HiBiT-FZD2-mCherry' follows the standard [N-tag]-[protein]-[C-tag] convention, placing HiBiT at the N-terminus. FZD2 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–23 (authoritative landmark); a tag upstream of residue 24 would be cleaved, so the junction is insert_after_residue=23, confirmed by reading seq[23]=A and seq[24]=Q from the numbered sequence. The mature N-terminus (residue 24) lies 222 residues from TM1 (246–268), well clear of any TM boundary. The C-terminus (residue 565) is intracellular, making residue 24 the only extracellular terminus and the topology-derived position unambiguous. Mouse HiBiT-FZD2-mCherry was stably integrated into U-2 OS cells (PMC12153800). The construct name places HiBiT at the N-terminus and mCherry at the C-terminus. FZD2's C-terminus (541–565) is intracellular, making the mature N-terminus (residue 24, after signal-peptide cleavage at 1–23) the sole extracellular terminus and the only topologically consistent position for the HiBiT tag.

sources.claim: Human embryonic kidney 293T (HEK293T) cells (CLS catalog number 300189), ΔFZD 1–10 HEK293 cells [ 21 ], U-2 OS cells (ATCC ® HTB-96 TM ) and U-2 OS cell lines with a stable integration of mouse HiBiT-FZD 1,2,4,5,7,8,9,10 -mCherry (generated in this project) were cultured in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle medium (Gibco, Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS, Thermo Fisher) and 1% penicillin–streptomycin (P/S; Gibco; Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA).

literature_notes: L1 (1D4-tagged mouse FZD2, Addgene #42264) does not qualify: the clip names no residue or terminus for the 1D4 tag, and 1D4 is conventionally placed at the C-terminus of GPCRs, which is intracellular for FZD2 (541–565). Because FZD2 has two termini (one extracellular, one intracellular), topology_derived derivation is not applicable to L1 — it would require knowing which terminus carries the tag, which the clip does not state. L3 lists HiBiT-FZD1,4,5,8,10-mCherry in NCI-H1703 cells but does not include FZD2 in that cell line; L2 (U-2 OS) is the direct FZD2 evidence. L4 demonstrates that HiBiT-FZD5 (same construct architecture) supports Wnt ligand-binding assays, providing indirect functional support for the design, but the functional result is not attributed to FZD2 and so does not raise the validation level above detected_only for this site.

literature_other_positions.note: mCherry is fused to the C-terminus of FZD2 in the HiBiT-FZD2-mCherry construct; residue 565 (V) falls within the intracellular C-terminal domain (541–565), so this is an intracellular fusion, not a surface tag site.
